title: proto: Replace format text()
description:
The proto.h APIs expect valid UTF-8 so replace uses of format_text()
with a label copy function that just does formatting and does not
check for encoding errors. Avoid multiple levels of temporary
string allocations.

Make sure the copy does not truncate a multibyte character and
produce invalid strings. Add debug checks for UTF-8 encoding errors
instead.

We escape C0 and C1 control codes (because control codes)
and ASCII whitespace (and bell).

Overall the goal is to be more efficient and optimized and help
detect misuse of APIs by passing invalid UTF-8.

Add a unit test for ws_label_strcat.

notes.body:
> Later we may want to generalize it to all of Unicode

The goal is to generate display strings that contain no control characters (other than a terminating NUL), so that all characters show up as *something* clearly visible rather than as, say some effect on the formatting due to a format effector.

So, yes, we would, at minimum, want to generalize it to the C1 control characters.  Combining characters are OK as foo followed by combining bar will show up as a foo+bar combination (and may all the gods of your people help you if it's [Zalgo text](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zalgo_text) :-)).

Heh, Zalgo text. Nice. Didn't know about that.

I added the C0 and C1 codes. :thumbsup:

At one point (3.0 and prior), `format_text()` expected ASCII, and replaced all non-ASCII characters with escapes. There are some uses of `format_text()` that still expect that behavior, notably anything that calls `get_dns_name()` (or DHCPv6's implementation of same). For functions that want all non ASCII to be escaped (or some other encoding), it doesn't produce the right result.

Probably the correct API is that `tvb_get_string_enc()` (and the direct "convert from this encoding functions in `epan/charsets`) should have an option to produce escaped bytes instead of replacement characters, as well as returning a boolean that indicates whether conversion to UTF-8 encountered no issues.

> For functions that want all non ASCII to be escaped (or some other encoding)

A character that's valid but not printable can be "escaped" so as to make it show up in a displayed string.

Is there some reason to show a character that's *not* valid in that fashion rather than as a REPLACEMENT CHARACTER?

Or should the process of generating the displayed string start with the *raw* string data, not the string data converted to UTF-8 and, for everything that's not valid, convert it to escaped byte values rather than a REPLACEMENT CHARACTER?
